question.text: Ferdinand and his wife were assassinated by this 19-year old Yugoslav nationalist. He was a member of the Black Hand, which planned Franz Ferdinand's assassination.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.leadin: The first democratically elected leader of this country was Sali Berisha.
swap.text: Identify this European nation whose past leaders have included King Zog and Enver Hoxha.
swap.clue: Its southern boundary is formed by the Pindus Mountains and its longest river is the Drin, which empties in the north.

question.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
question.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
question.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

swap.text: This former president of Yugoslavia was put on trial for crimes against humanity, but he died during the proceedings at the Hague. He allegedly committed genocide in Kosovo.
swap.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about conferences held in Berlin during the late 19th century.
question.text: The 1878 conference also allowed Austria-Hungary to occupy this territory. A later event in this territory led to Austria-Hungary issuing the July Ultimatum.
question.clue: The Stanak assembly governed a kingdom named for this country, founded by Tvrtko I of the Kotromanic dynasty, until its 1464 conquest.

swap.text: The newest member of the EU is this country which joined in 2013. Its leader, Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic works in its Presidential palace at Zagreb.
swap.clue: This country was merged with Slavonia in 1868, though Rijeka ] remained separate.

question.leadin: This man formed the Non-Aligned Movement with Nasser and Nehru.
question.text: Identify this man who led his country to become the only member of Cominform to repel Soviet domination.
question.clue: Fitzroy Maclean was this man's British liaison, and this ruler fought against the Ustasha and his nemesis Draza Mihailovic, leader of the Nazi-collaborationist Chetnik movement.

swap.leadin: Basil II had the longest reign of any leader of his empire, revitalizing it over his nearly 50-year rule.
swap.text: Basil is known as the "slayer" of this ethnic group for ending their first empire at the Battle of Kleidion in 1014 and having 99 of every 100 prisoners fully blinded and the remaining left with one eye.
swap.answerHtml: Bulgars [do not accept or prompt on “Bulgarians,” as that is a distinct modern ethnic group]
swap.clue: High taxes under this people's ruler Peter I may have prompted the rise of Bogomilism.

question.text: In the 1960s, this country outlawed abortion and imposed taxes on childless adults in an effort to increase its population under a Communist leader killed after a Christmas day trial in 1989.
question.clue: Ethnic violence broke out during the fall of communism in Tirgu Mures and was centered on its Hungarian minority.

swap.text: Although never technically holding office as head of state, this communist led Albania from 1944 to 1985, after forging an anti-Italian alliance with the Balli Kombetar.
swap.clue: A vocal opponent of Mao (+) Zedong's "three worlds" theory, this man was abandoned by his closest ally, China, and successfully imposed state atheism despite his country's majority Muslim population.

question.leadin: Ante Pavelic served as the Poglavnik of this organization from 1941 to 1945.
question.text: Name this fascist organization that ruled a Nazi puppet state from Zagreb. One member of this organization was known for keeping a jar of eyeballs on his desk.
question.answerHtml: Ustaše (us-TA-shay) [accept but do NOT otherwise reveal Ustaša (us-TA-sha) – Croatian Revolutionary Movement; accept but do Not otherwise reveal Ustaša – Hrvatski revolucionarni pokret; do NOT accept or prompt on “Croatia”]
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.text: Starting in the mid-1960s, he served as dictator of Romania.
swap.clue: This man held back his country from participating in the Warsaw Pact invasion of Prague.

question.text: The Cyrillic script, which later supplanted Glagolitic, was developed in this empire during the rule of Tsar Simeon I. Another branch of this empire formed a namesake state on the Volga river in the 9th century CE.
question.clue: From the 7th century onwards, the empire fought a series of wars with this state for control of Thrace and Greece. In the 10th century, this state reached its greatest territorial extent under Simeon I.

swap.leadin: It's not Turkey, but the term "Pomaks" is used to refer to Muslims who live in this country, whose Muslims, along with ethnic Greeks, agitated for an Ottoman occupation of Western Thrace in the 1910s.
swap.text: Name this country. Sixty years after abolishing its monarchy, this country elected its final King Simeon II as Prime Minister.
swap.clue: This country pursued the Treaty of Craiova to recover territory lost in the Treaty of Neuilly, its "second national catastrophe," which saw it lose Southern Dobruja.

question.leadin: This man defended the castle of Kruja several times.
question.text: Name this former captain who defected from the services of the Ottoman Sultan to found the League of Lezhe (LEH-zhuh). He is known by a corruption of a Turkish title which translates into English as "Lord Alexander."
question.answerHtml: George Kastrioti Skanderbeg [or Gjergj Kastrioti Skënderbeu; or İskender Bey]
question.clue: Pope Calixtus II chose this man to be Captain General of the Holy See in 1457.

swap.leadin: Name the following 20th century eastern European leaders.
swap.text: This patron of Nicolae Ceausescu was the Communist leader of Romania from 1948 to 1965. Domestically, he emphasized the manufacturing of consumer goods, while he sought to improve foreign relations with both the West and China.
swap.clue: Together with Petru Groza, this Romanian leader reportedly held King Michael at gunpoint to convince him to abdicate. After becoming prime minister in 1952, he forged alliances with China and other non-communist states, before being succeeded as party leader by Nicolae Ceausescu ("chow-SHES-koo").

question.text: Along with Milosevic, this neofascist Croatian dictator was party to the earlier 1995 Dayton Accords, which allowed for the NATO implementation force to take over for U.N. peacekeepers in Bosnia.
question.clue: This president of Croatia throughout most of the 1990s. He signed the Erdut Agreement with the remaining independent republics and thus fully achieved Croatian independence.

swap.text: The hygiene practices of the lazaret were adopted from quarantine practices of this historical state that controlled much of Dalmatia until the 19th century. It was centered on the modern-day city of Dubrovnik.
swap.clue: This home state of Mavro Orbini. This maritime republic pioneered public health measures like the trentina, a mandatory 30-day quarantine for travelers, and suffered a devastating 1667 earthquake.

question.leadin: This time lasted from 1948 to 1954 and was named for the organization controlled by Stalin which Yugoslavia did not wish to join.
question.text: Identify this period, during which Yugoslavia's refusal to join the Warsaw Pact led to the constant threat of Soviets deposing the Yugoslavian leadership.
question.clue: This period during which over 100 citizens were killed at the Goli Otok ("GOH-lee OH-toke") prison camp. The Belgrade declaration ended this seven-year period with a rapprochement between the Soviet Union and another nation.

swap.leadin: After this man was diagnosed with polycythemia, he joked that he was "suffering from an excess of reds."
swap.text: What Archbishop was controversially put on trial by Tito and convicted for treason for his relationship with the Ustase government during World War II? While eventually released from prison, he died soon after and was declared a martyr years later by Pope John Paul II.
